persistence.policy: No silent downgrade. Old readers reject the new versions. Removing a lane does not downgrade a project. pre-programmed needs explicit parser/rendering parity before it can play the new formats.

target.initialScope: One two-point lane on a piano-roll synth instrument; unsupported instrument types reject instead of silently ignoring the lane

points.identity: Two stable IDs, increasing integer sixteenth-note steps on the Beat clock
points.interpolation: Exponential in Hz, linear in octaves; exact endpoints
points.outsideRange: Hold first value before begin; hold last after end
points.smoothing: No extra smoothing or hidden UI timer; the explicit exponential segment is the transition
points.ordering: Increasing musical position; simultaneous authored points reject. Compiled boundary events use stable order and distinct boundary/point namespaces.

precedence: Patch base cutoff if there is no lane
Beat-clock timeline cutoff replaces the base when a lane exists
Per-note legacy tone, legacy sweep and canonical modulation apply after the timeline base
Final host filter frequency is bounded to Nyquist
legacySweep: On automated voices, a separate detune control multiplies the timeline base by the authored per-note sweep. Native still explicitly rejects sweep and legacy LFO/tone until their own parity work is complete.

clock.unit: 60 / actual transport BPM / 4 seconds per step
clock.chunk: The lane spans the Beat clock and never restarts at Chunk boundaries
clock.song: Each referenced Beat iteration uses its own local step; Song BPM determines seconds. Clip/Beat end values hold through release tails.
clock.loop: New cycle voices restart the lane; older release tails keep their terminal cutoff
clock.seek: New notes evaluate the lane at the actual seek position, including a seek into the middle of the segment. Existing onset-based transport does not chase/reconstruct voices that began before the seek.
clock.edits: Scheduled voices retain their immutable plan. Edits are heard on newly scheduled notes or the next playback pass; no live automation recording or mid-note plan replacement is claimed.

rendering.browser: Compiled absolute-time AudioParam exponential ramps in the existing filter graph
rendering.native: Bounded six-point curve in the same C++ Voice, evaluated at sample time before modulation; no audio-thread allocation, JSON or I/O
rendering.offline: Beat/Song WAV uses the same render events and compiled voice plans; no normalization/limiting behavior was added
rendering.callback: Offline and allocation/block assertions do not establish device latency, underruns or callback deadlines

interface.entry: move over time next to the existing Cutoff control
interface.editing: Two begin/end rows with bar, beat and Hz values; remove and undo use the canonical project mutation path
interface.presets: Timeline automation is stored in the Beat, not a sound preset
interface.incompatibleChanges: Remove cutoff movement before changing an automated instrument to a rack or recording

remaining: Live replacement of already scheduled voice plans
Reference hardware/device and human musical/newcomer evaluation
